experiment: stop one of two ALB targets with EC2 StopInstances

comparison.claim: After the fault, the surviving path internet -> ALB -> web-b still flows and the path through web-a no longer does: the service stays reachable and every request is served by web-b.
comparison.evidence: all 151 requests in the final 30 s were 200 from web-b (baseline served by [web-a web-b])

comparison.claim: The simulation verdict for losing one instance is "unaffected": no entry point loses its path to stateful storage.
comparison.evidence: the run does not test this claim

comparison.claim: The ALB stops sending traffic to the stopped instance within 30 s of it ceasing to respond: 2 consecutive failed checks at one check every 10 s, plus at most one interval of phase. Until then some requests (about half, with two targets) fail.
comparison.evidence: failures spanned 26.2 s (bound 30 s); 51% of requests in that window failed (predicted about half)

comparison.claim: Once the instance reaches the stopped state the target group reports it as unused with reason Target.InvalidState (not unhealthy).
